text:
carmen: quick flag while onboarding cust Nectar's adapter (nectar-lora-2.3). Running invoice evalpack on int4 and seeing trailing-zero elision and occasional dropped negative signs in currency spans. anyone free to take a look?

jiro: curious. paste one redacted fail?

carmen: here's a tiny repro (redacted):

```
input: "Total due: -$2,400.00"
expected: "Total due: -$2,400.00"
model (fp16): "Total due: -$2,400.00"
model (int4): "Total due: 2,400"  <-- minus gone, cents dropped
```

jiro: that smells like tokenizer graft + quantized decode noise. Which tokenizer merge did you use?

carmen: merge used "nectar-graft-currencypack" on top of base-en-v3. We added a handful of currency subtokens to reduce split tokens for amounts.

eval-bot: quick evalpack run: 120 samples, variants: graft+int4, graft+int8, base-only+int4. Summary: graft+int4: 14/120 currency-format errors; graft+int8: 1/120; base-only+int4: 2/120. Artifacts: s3://redwood-eval/nectar/nectar-lora-2.3/1791112223/

jiro: can you dump the token stream for a failing example (tokenize -> detok pre/postproc)?

carmen: token dump for one bad case:

```
# tokens (grafted): [22, 4100, 9997, 88, 304, 777]
# detok before postproc: "Total due: - 2 400 . 0 0"
# postproc -> "-2,400.00"
# int4 decode -> "2,400"
```

jiro: interesting-- the minus and trailing 0 seem to be decoded as lower-prob tokens under int4. Two quick experiments to triage: 1) re-run with `--force-postproc` in runtime to ensure postproc isn't skipped in fallback paths; 2) compare beam-size=1 vs beam=4 to see if scoring chooses a shorter tokenization.

carmen: kicking those off now: `./evalpack --samples 120 --quant=int4 --force-postproc --beam=4`

eval-bot: follow-up run: force-postproc fixed 9/14; beam=4 recovered 3 more; 2 cases remain. Latency int4 ~ -17% vs fp16. CI: https://ci.internal.redwood/run/9421

jiro: so it's a combined effect: grafted subtokens create a tokenization that in noisy logits can prefer removing punctuation or digits. Recommendations: 1) short-term pin Nectar to int8 for production; 2) add a decode-time bias for currency/punctuation tokens when a numeric span is detected; 3) schedule a focused quant calibration sweep that includes grafted currency tokens so quant preserves logit margins for those tokens.

carmen: will open a ticket and pin canary to int8. ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/ML-1410

infra-bot: scheduled canary pin for nectar-lora-2.3 -> int8 on stack-9 at 1791112239.

jiro: also add a small unit check in the graft merge CI: 50-sample numeric-format smoke with int4 to catch regressions pre-canary.

carmen: adding test now, will ping when green. thanks! :thumbsup:
